articles.title: Fleetwood 1-0 Tranmere
articles.summary: Captain Shaun Rooney's 82nd-minute winner earned a 1-0 Sky Bet League Two win for Carabao Cup quarter-finalists Fleetwood over Tranmere.
articles.body:
Rooney converted an Andy Cannon corner, which was just reward for the home side's second-half dominance.

The Fylde Coast outfit had not beaten Rovers since 2019, going four league games since then without a goal until the skipper's late intervention.

The Cod Army's three points lifted them up to 11th in the table, two points adrift of the play-offs.

While the game will not live long in the memory, Matt Lawlor's side was good value for the victory.

Rooney produced Town's first effort with a rising drive after 17 minutes, while team-mate Jake Batty was only denied by the legs of Tranmere goalkeeper Luke McGee.

Rovers, who drop one place to 15th after the defeat, went closest after a 27th-minute goalmouth scramble, with George Nevett's header forcing Jay Lynch to save on to the crossbar.

But only one team looked likely to prevail after half-time as Crispin McLean forced another save from McGee.

With the game heading for a stalemate, Rooney's second goal of the season proved the difference.

articles.title: Spain vs England: Spain boss Luis de la Fuente says no racism in Spanish football
articles.summary: Spain manager Luis de la Fuente says "there is no racism in Spain" and England boss Thomas Tuchel reiterates that he does not believe it will be an issue at Sunday's Nations League meeting in Madrid.
articles.body:
Luis de la Fuente has dismissed concerns over racism in Spanish football before the national team's Uefa Nations League meeting with England in Madrid on Sunday.

Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel had earlier confirmed he would remind his players of Uefa's anti-racism protocol before the fixture, which will determine who finishes top of League A Group 3.

While he has stressed he didn't expect there to be any incidents, the visit will be England's first to the Spanish capital since a notorious 2004 encounter at the Bernabeu was overshadowed by racist chanting directed at their players.

Spain head coach De la Fuente was asked whether Tuchel's message to his players showed there was still work needed to tackle racism in Spain.

But he responded: "What I'd tell you, and you can tell Thomas, is that in Spain, there's no racism.

"Just like that, crystal clear. Just like in England, there's no racism in Spain. We aren't racist, any of us."

The Spanish Football Federation was fined last month and ordered to partially close a stadium after supporters directed Islamophobic and xenophobic chants towards Muslims during a match against Egypt in Barcelona.

In the domestic game, Real Madrid's Brazilian forward Vinicius Jr has been a vocal anti-racism campaigner after frequently being on the end of racist chanting - and worse. In 2024 three Valencia fans were sentenced to eight months in prison for abusing him at a match.

Uefa operates a three-step protocol, allowing referees to stop matches, take players off the pitch temporarily and, ultimately, abandon a game if discriminatory behaviour continues.

Tuchel said on Friday: "Maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent [in Madrid]. And then, yeah, we will give our answers if stuff like this happens. Best answers are on the pitch."

However, when asked again about his views at a pre-match news conference on Saturday, Tuchel added: "I never talk about racism in Spain.

"I answered politely a question about what happens, I never expect racism. I got asked, 'what will happen if and if and if?'. And I said, 'if it happens, there's a protocol in place'. That's it.

"But my trust is that we have a friendly atmosphere, that we have an atmosphere who is clearly in favour of the Spanish team, and that football does what it does best: brings people together and not divide people."

Midfielder Declan Rice said: "In the past, I've experienced that in Montenegro and Bulgaria and there was a protocol in place that we followed - we came off the pitch. We know exactly where we are as a group on that.

"The times we are in now, 2026, there should never be racism in football. It's shocking we still have it in the game today.

"I don't want to think about if one of our players or their players is racially abused because that would be a horrible mark on football."

Focusing on the match itself, De la Fuente believed both teams are currently at the pinnacle of world football, although he rejected the suggestion one could simply replicate the other's playing style.

Spain were crowned World Cup winners in the summer, while England finished third after losing to Argentina in the semi-finals.

"I prefer the Spanish model. It's very recognisable, the players are perfectly adapted," said De la Fuente. "The English model is very good, but you have to have that type of player. Neither England can play like Spain, nor Spain like England."

He suggested Spain had faced increasingly aggressive opposition as their recent success had raised expectations.

"It's our best moment in a long time," added De la Fuente, whose side also lifted the Euro 2024 title by beating England. "They are all much more aggressive to beat us now than in other times."

He also defended the value of Spanish players, arguing their performances often outweighed their transfer-market prices compared with those in the Premier League.

"Spanish footballers surprise me that, compared to what is paid in England, they are very cheap," he explained. "I see them as better, in my opinion. Everyone in their market can set the prices."

On the fitness of forward Lamine Yamal, he remained cautious over whether the Barcelona teenager would start or how long he could manage.

"We will see if he is a starter, but if he comes out, it's because he's fit to play," said De la Fuente.

articles.title: Wales Nations League: What Craig Bellamy need to stay in top tier
articles.summary: BBC Sport Wales explains how Wales can stay in the Nations League top tier despite finishing bottom of their group.
articles.body:
It can be easy to get tangled up in the complexities of Nations League permutations and, although Wales still have a few uncertainties to iron out, the picture is becoming clearer for Craig Bellamy's side.

Following their 3-1 defeat in Norway on Saturday, Wales will finish bottom of Group A4 even if they win their final game against reigning champions Portugal on Tuesday.

But that does not mean they will definitely be relegated from the top tier.

Instead, they are almost certain to play one of the teams from League B in a relegation play-off in March.

However, one thing is for sure: As a result of the Norway loss, Wales will not be among the top seeds for Euro 2028 qualifying.

"We wanted to be in pot one. That was the drive," said head coach Bellamy after the defeat in Oslo.

"Some people might say, 'what makes you think you should be in pot one?' But I do.

"Maybe I'm naïve. I see in big parts of that game we can be in pot one. Let's take the good bits from the game, definitely improve on certain moments of the game and just keep pushing."

How certain that Wales will be in a relegation play-off?

A point against Portugal would make sure of it, but even if they lose, Wales will most likely end up in a relegation play-off.

Only the two worst-performing sides will be automatically relegated to League B.

With one game left, the other bottom teams in League A - Turkey, the Czech Republic and Serbia - all have no points, whereas Wales have three.

For them to finish among the worst two, they would need to lose to Portugal, and two of the other teams would need to win their final fixture with a significant swing in goal difference.

Wales have a goal difference of -5. Considering Turkey (-10) visit France, Czech Republic (-10) are in Croatia and Serbia (-7) travel to Greece, it would require an unlikely turn of events for Bellamy's men to be automatically relegated.

The relegation play-offs will be held across two legs at the end of March, with the first leg between March 25-27, and the second between March 28-30.

As a League A side, Wales will be seeded and therefore play at home in the second leg.

The draw for the play-offs takes place at Uefa's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland, on Friday, 20 November.

The sides that finish in the top two of League A's four groups will also discover the quarter-final draw on the same day.

With one game left to play, it's not yet clear.

Slovenia, Northern Ireland, Kosovo and Bosnia-Herzegovina are currently all in second place in their groups.

However, Scotland, Ukraine, Austria, the Republic of Ireland and Poland could also be potential opponents.

Where does Euro 2028 qualifying come into this?

All teams finishing third or higher in League A will be named as top seeds for Euro 2028 qualifying.

By missing out, Wales could now be drawn alongside one of Europe's heavyweights in their group.

Spain, France, Italy, Netherlands and Portugal are among the sides already guaranteed pot one seeding for the draw on 6 December in Belfast.

England will also be a top seed, although Thomas Tuchel's men will be kept apart from Wales and the other Euro 2028 co-hosts in qualifying regardless.

When it comes to reaching the Euros, the 12 group winners and eight best-ranked runners-up qualify directly.

For any of the co-hosts who don't make it via that route, there are two automatic spots available. Those will be awarded to the best-ranked between the four nations who haven't qualified directly.

If Wales still haven't made it, there is still the back-up option of the play-offs.

And given play-off places are based on Nations League rankings, Wales are highly likely to already have that safety net.

articles.title: After another blowout win, where does Wake Forest fit in College Football Playoff picture?
articles.summary: The Demon Deacons bullied SMU all game and sent a message to the CFP committee.
articles.body:
Sooner or later, the College Football Playoff selection committee needs to start respecting Wake Forest.

Put the biases aside. Forget history. Just watch the games. Does that look like the 13 th best team in the country to you?

Granted, for a variety of reasons, it's hard to tell where Wake Forest exactly fits in the hierarchy of this unpredictable 2026 season. It's not their fault the ACC has become a sad football conference and that there are a bunch of teams that could also be 9-1 with this schedule.

But just look at what this team is doing to opponents lately — if you can stomach the carnage. Every week, Wake Forest shows up to play a football game. And every week, the team they're playing has unwittingly signed up for a humiliation ritual.

Sure, strength of schedule matters. But so does kicking ass — and in a year defined by parity across the country, nobody is doing it as thoroughly as the Demon Deacons.

By halftime Saturday in Dallas, Wake Forest had so completely disemboweled SMU that you wonder why anyone — including the Mustangs players — bothered showing up for the second half. At that point, the game was already 42-0 on the way to a 49-7 finish . It might have been the most lopsided game of the year between two pretty good teams.

And yes, SMU was considered a pretty good team at 7-2 before turning into chum for the insatiable sharks wearing gold helmets. But SMU shouldn't feel too bad. Since squeaking by Louisville on Sept. 26, Wake Forest has done this to everyone .

In its last six games, the Deacs have outscored their opponents by a combined 313-38. Sure, there are some results in there that won't move the needle as far as the playoff picture (a 77-0 win over Merrimack in early November is only a statement that Wake Forest should have scheduled better), but 51-7 over Virginia? Beating Stanford 57-3? And then backing it up at SMU with a game that was effectively over well before halftime?

Those aren't great or necessarily even good teams, but Wake is no fluke. We should have already known that back in mid-September when the Demon Deacons suffered their only loss — a very competitive 33-20 decision at Miami. Wake Forest wasn't necessarily close to winning that game, but they looked like they could match up physically — which is crucial, since Miami is the only playoff-caliber team they'll see all year.

Since then, all Wake Forest has done is show time and time again that what happened against Miami was legitimate.

When you are routinely beating conference opponents like this, even in a mediocre conference, it says you belong. And if Wake finishes the regular season at 11-1, which they are very likely to do with games remaining against Georgia Tech and Duke at home, they unequivocally deserve a chance to be in the playoff no matter what happens in a potential ACC championship game rematch with Miami.

So far, they're skeptical. At No. 13 this week, Wake Forest was behind several two-loss teams, including BYU and Kentucky, It's even ranked lower than one-loss Texas Tech, which got destroyed at Cincinnati and subsequently survived fourth quarter battles against Arizona and West Virginia.

It's easy to understand why. This particular committee places a high value on quality wins, and Wake Forest doesn't have one that pops off the page. Nobody is going to say it explicitly, but after years of the SEC complaining about strength of schedule not getting enough credit in the room, it feels like the committee has finally been browbeaten into submission.

Let's say Wake Forest wins its final two games and loses another close one to Miami in the ACC championship game to finish 11-2. It would be a big statement — perhaps even the kind of statement the committee wants to make about scheduling heading into the 24-team era — if Wake Forest got left out under those circumstances.

But it would also be an unfortunate misreading of what the playoff was expanded for in the first place.

Just like Indiana two years ago, which got in at 11-1 without beating a ranked team, it's OK to question if the win-loss record is telling an accurate story about Wake Forest. But that's what the playoff is for, and that's why it expanded a few years ago. With 12 slots available, there has to be enough room in the field for a power conference team that has only lost to a true national title contender and largely dominated everyone else.

If that means a pretty good three-loss SEC team gets left out, too bad. Let Greg Sankey go whine about it on Paul Finebaum's show.

In general, the problem with the committee is that it can't just do one thing or value one metric. The college football season is a big jigsaw puzzle with a bunch of different-sized pieces.

You can't just focus on win-loss records because schedules matter, and they vary wildly from conference to conference, and you'll inevitably end up with teams that don't belong there. But you also can't just focus on strength of schedule because winning games has to matter, too. And you can't just focus on head-to-head because if you apply that principle to every comparison between teams, you'll wind up in a mental pretzel.

The truth is that the committee's job is to pull a little bit on each of those threads and make some very tough decisions. Trotting out these rankings every week when they have a very incomplete set of data sets them up for constant criticism because, inevitably, the logic used to rank one team over another will not apply to a different ranking.

It makes the committee look inconsistent and wishy-washy, but realistically, it makes them normal. Sometimes, the unsatisfactory answer comes down to, "We think Team X has done a better job of navigating its schedule than Team Y." And that's perfectly acceptable when there's no real way to compare two teams that have traveled very different paths. That's what the committee is there for — to process the game like human beings, not computers.

That's also the problem with Wake Forest, though, particularly in a year where there may be a strength-of-schedule backlash brewing in the committee room: There's no other team like them in the country. Because of the week-in, week-out dominance, but also because of a schedule that isn't going to look as good as the playoff contenders in the SEC or Big Ten, they're forcing the committee to guess.

Does their physicality up front, their ballhawking defense and their elite offensive play-calling in ACC games translate to the national championship picture? Ultimately, unless Wake can win an automatic bid with the ACC title, it'll be up to the committee to decide.

So far, it seems they've got plenty of questions about whether this is truly a playoff-worthy team. But every time Wake Forest has played football for nearly two months, they've been screaming the answer.

articles.title: NBC pays tribute to Dan Hicks before coverage of Notre Dame vs. Boston College broadcast
articles.summary: Hicks called play-by-play for Notre Dame football on NBC for a combined seven seasons from 2013 to 2026.
articles.body:
Before its broadcast of Notre Dame's home matchup with Boston College on Saturday, NBC paid tribute to Dan Hicks, who called Fighting Irish games on the network for a combined seven seasons.

Hicks died on Wednesday at the age of 64 while dealing with an acute illness.

Studio host Ahmed Fareed began Saturday's coverage by expressing his admiration and sympathy on behalf of colleagues and friends "still in shock" over Hicks' death.

"Today we will celebrate a man whose expertise, but more importantly his warmth and his humor, will live on through everyone he knew," Fareed said, his voice quivering with emotion. "So this is not just another game for us, not just another day. Today is a day that we remember and miss our friend."

"Our broadcast booth feels very hollow right now, here at NBC Sports," Jason Benetti said as the network's telecast of Notre Dame's game with Boston College began. "I wish I wasn't here right now," he added. "I wish Dan was here right now."

Jason Garrett, Hicks' broadcast partner on NBC's Notre Dame broadcasts since 2024, credited the veteran announcer for always looking out for him as they worked. He often asked, "Can I tee you up?"

"What I always loved about Hicksy is it never was about him," said Garrett. "It was always about embracing the moment and highlighting the people involved, and that's how he lived his life."

"As legendary a broadcaster as he was, he was a better guy," he continued. "Devoted husband and father and friend. He was always so generous to me. He had an amazing spirit, he brightened every room he was in."

Jimmy Roberts, who worked with Hicks for years on NBC's golf coverage, introduced a video tribute package that showed the breadth of Hicks' career.

"The depth of our sorrow usually mirrors the depth of our love. That makes sense," Roberts said. "What makes no sense at all is that Dan isn't in South Bend today doing what he loved to do and doing it as well as anybody has ever done it."

Roberts narrated the tribute package which included clips from him calling football, golf, tennis, Olympic swimming and skiing, in addition to anchoring studio coverage, interviews and talk show appearances.

"He was everywhere in his three decades here. He did it all because he could do it all," Roberts said in his narration.

"How many people possessed that type of versatility?" Roberts continued. "The truth is, so few could make something so complicated, and often chaotic, look so easy. That was his superpower. That, and the way he made people feel."

Hicks called play-by-play for Notre Dame football on NBC for a combined seven seasons from 2013 to 2026. His career with the network began in 1992, broadcasting the NFL.

articles.title: El Sant Andreu gana el derbi al Europa... ¡ante 16.430 espectadores!
articles.standfirst: Un doblete de Alexis decidió el duelo, disputado en el RCDE Stadium
articles.summary: Un doblete de Alexis decidió el duelo, disputado en el RCDE Stadium
articles.body: Fiesta grande del fútbol barcelonés en un escenario de Primera División donde más de 16.000 personas de ambas aficiones se dieron cita en el RCDE Stadium, decidiéndose el encuentro por un doblete del cuatribarrado Alexis. La primera parte estuvo marcada por el respeto, disponiendo el Europa de la primera ocasión en una acción a balón parado en la que Khalid estuvo muy cerca de inaugurar el marcador. La respuesta cuatribarrada llegó con un disparo de Jeremy desde fuera del área que rozó el larguero. A partir de ahí se mantuvo la intensidad, aunque las ocasiones de peligro fueron escasas, teniendo Bermejo la última oportunidad antes del descanso. Tras el paso por los vestuarios, los escapulados saltaron mejor al campo en una segunda mitad presidida por la lluvia. Un contragolpe de manual tras un robo de balón de Jeremy permitió a Alexis culminar la jugada, asistido por Jaume Tovar, para hacer el 0-1. Posteriormente, Tito Tolosa pudo ampliar la cuenta, pero Nil Ruiz lo evitó con una gran intervención. Flavio rozó el empate con un disparo, y la réplica la puso Bermejo, volviendo a topar con el guardameta del Europa. En el minuto 84, el colegiado anuló un gol a Alexis por fuera de juego en primera instancia, pero tras consultar el VAR lo dio como válido. Los de Luis Blanco lo intentaron hasta el final para revertir la situación, pero el Sant Andreu se defendió con solidez y supo gestionar su renta. Europa: Nil Ruiz; Álex Cano, Sgrò (Cancelo, 80’), Campeny; Flavio, Gori, Víctor Morales (Tito Tolosa, 69’), Padillo (Cadenas, 80’); Mascaró (Youssef, 61’), Teto Martín (Exposito, 61’) y Khalid. Sant Andreu: Ramón Juan; Jordi Méndez, Andreu, Montoro, Lucas Viña (Nil, 83’); Marc Delgado (Torices, 58’), Alexis, Pau Darbra (Carrasco, 67’); Jeremy (Agudín, 67’), Bermejo y Jaume Tovar (Albertito, 83’). Goles: 0-1 (64’): Alexis. 0-2 (84’): Alexis. Árbitro: Román Román, del colegio leonés. Amonestó a los locales Sgrò y Expósito; y a los visitantes Andreu, Bermejo, Jeremy y Marc Delgado. Roja al preparador físico del Sant Andreu (45’+). Campo: RCDE Stadium. Un total de 16.430 espectadores.

articles.title: Portugal no está para homenajes
articles.standfirst: Dinamarca goleó en el Municipal de Braga en el primer partido de la 'seleçao' sin Cristiano
articles.summary: Dinamarca goleó en el Municipal de Braga en el primer partido de la 'seleçao' sin Cristiano
articles.body: Hay partidos que siempre quedan grabados en los libros de historia de una selección. Éste era el primero de Portugal sin Cristiano Ronaldo después de 23 años de servicio intachable. Dinamarca, sin embargo, se encargó de 'reventar' la fiesta montada en el Municipal de Braga. No era un once cualquiera. Era el primero de una nueva era en Portugal. El debutante Alberto Costa entró directo al once para ocupar el lateral derecho de la defensa; Vitinha y Rúben Neves formaron pareja en el doble pivote; y Gonçalo Ramos ejerció como '9' por delante de una línea de mediapuntas donde se encontraban Pedro Neto, Bruno Fernandes y Joao Félix. Hjulmand fue titular en la sala de máquinas de Noruega. Salieron todos vistiendo una camiseta con el mítico '7' de Cristiano y, a los siete minutos, los presentes en el Municipal de Braga se pusieron en pie para brindarle un sonoro aplauso. En los videomarcadores, además, se proyectaron imágenes y un mensaje donde podía leerse 'obrigado, capitán' ('gracias, capitán'). Portugal, sin embargo, saltó bastante fría y espesa al terreno de juego. Con Bruno Fernandes tirado a banda izquierda y Joao Félix ejerciendo como '10' por detrás de Gonçalo Ramos, los de Jorge Jesus no eran capaces de agarrar el balón y poder salir progresando de su propio campo. A raíz de dos disparos lejanos a cargo de Vitinha y Neto que no pusieron en problemas a Hermansen, Portugal comenzó a entonarse. Al menos, le dio la vuelta a la posesión y se instaló en campo rival. En el 38', sin embargo, Dinamarca ya avisó con un tanto anulado por fuera de juego de Damsgaard en el origen y, acto seguido, Rúben Dias cometió un penalti tras bloquear con la mano un 'cabezazo' de Hojlund. Lo leyó Diogo Costa... pero no falló Hojbjerg. Potente y arriba. Para colmo, Rúben Dias fue amonestado nada más arrancar la segunda parte y se perderá el partido final contra Gales. No fue, eso sí, lo peor para Portugal. En el 49', Damsgaard recibió dentro del área, pudo darse la vuelta... y sirvió un envío al segundo palo que Hojlund 'empaló' de primeras. Nada pudo hacer Diogo Costa. Trató de recomponerse Portugal con un 'zapatazo' de Rúben Neves que Hermansen se quitó de encima como pudo. Neto mandó el rechace arriba. Quien no volvió a perdonar, en el 56', fue Hojlund. Recibió en tres cuartos, rompió a Renato Veiga y la clavó con la derecha al palo largo. Rúben Dias, que rompía el fuera de juego, se quedó enganchado. Jorge Jesus, de inmediato, realizó un triple cambio. Entraron Palhinha, Trincao, que mandó arriba el primer balón que tocó a pase de Vitinha, y un Carlos Forbs que heredaba el '7'... aunque ya lo vistió hace un año en un partido contra Armenia de clasificación en Mundial. Pero, lejos de haber reacción, Dinamarca aumentó la goleada a falta de un cuarto de hora. La puso Hjulmand de falta y Joachim Andersen cabeceó de forma inapelable. El homenaje a Cristiano fue para olvidar y necesitarán empatar contra Gales para cerrar el grupo como líderes. Portugal, al menos, logró maquillar el marcador en el descuento. Forbs desbordó por derecha, Hermansen sacó el disparo de Joao Neves desde el corazón del área... pero Bernardo Silva estuvo atento para recoge el rechace.

articles.title: Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith breaks Big Ten's all-time receiving record in win over Northwestern
articles.summary: Smith accomplished the feat on a 22-yard catch and run in the first quarter on Saturday.
articles.body:
Jeremiah Smith can catch pretty much anything, or anyone apparently. On Saturday, late in the first quarter of a 28-19 win over Northwestern, the Ohio State junior wide receiver surpassed Purdue's John Standeford for the Big Ten's all-time receiving record.

Over four seasons from 2000-03, Standeford piled up 3,788 receiving yards. In less than three seasons with the No. 20 Buckeyes, Smith eclipsed that mark.

He climbed to the top of the Big Ten leaderboard in that department with a 22-yard catch and run against the Wildcats in Ohio Stadium.

Smith went on to author his 17th career 100-yard receiving game, tied with Purdue's David Bell and Michigan's Braylon Edwards for the most a Big Ten player has ever notched. He was targeted 17 times in a Buckeyes win that snapped their uncharacteristic two-game losing streak. Along the way, he caught 11 balls for 117 yards and one touchdown.

He now has a Big Ten-best 3,875 career receiving yards.

Even before Saturday's game, the 6-foot-4, 222-pound Smith held the record for the most career receiving touchdowns in Big Ten history. He entered the weekend with 41 of those. Two weeks ago at USC, he leapfrogged Edwards, who wrapped his four-season run at Michigan (2001-04) with 39 receiving TDs.

If you're wondering, Purdue's Taylor Stubblefield is the Big Ten's all-time leader in receptions. He logged 325 from 2001-04.

After the Northwestern game, Smith's up to 243 career catches. Given that he's widely projected as a top pick in next year's NFL Draft , it's unlikely the Miami Gardens, Florida, native will stick around to grab that record.

Besides, he's already responsible for one triple crown. Smith ranks first in the Ohio State record books for career receiving yards, receiving touchdowns and receptions.

He snatched all three of those records this season, in which he's currently the favorite to win the Heisman Trophy.

During the infancy of the 2026 campaign, on Sept. 19 versus Kent State, Smith hopped Michael Jenkins for the Buckeyes' all-time receiving yards record . Jenkins amassed 2,898 receiving yards while at Ohio State in the early 2000s.

Then, on Oct. 3 at Iowa, Smith zoomed by two more recent Buckeyes receivers . He overtook Chris Olave (35 TD receptions) for the most career touchdown catches in program history, and he exceeded Emeka Egbuka's 205 career receptions, which were previously the most an Ohio State player had ever tallied.

Jenkins, Olave and Egbuka were all first-round picks. They're just a few of the several receivers who make up a fraternity of prolific Buckeyes wideouts.

Smith is among them, and it's hard to argue that he's not the best of them. He's a two-time All-American and a one-time national champion, and he puts up big numbers just about all the time, even after an unexpected quarterback change .

articles.title: Suecia y Austria regresan a la élite
articles.standfirst: Las dos selecciones ascienden a la Liga A de la Nations League
articles.summary: Las dos selecciones ascienden a la Liga A de la Nations League
articles.body: La quinta jornada de la Nations League dejó dos buenas noticias en forma de ascenso: Austria y Suecia regresan a la Liga A. Austria, sin el exmadridista David Alaba, lesionado, ha ganado por la mínima a la República de Irlanda (1-0). Un gol del 'gigantón' Sasa Kalajdzic -remató sobre la línea un córner botado por Romano Schmid y prolongado por Michael Gregoritsch- valió para derrotar al combinado del bético Troy Parrot, titular. A falta de una jornada, Austria ya es inalcanzable. Los pupilos de Ralf Rangnick son ya inalcanzables para el resto. Lideran el Grupo 3 de la Liga B con cinco puntos de ventaja sobre Kosovo, seis sobre Irlanda y ocho sobre Israel. También ascendió Suecia después de una sufrida victoria sobre Bosnia y Herzegovina (3-2). Y eso que ganaba 3-0 al descanso gracias a los tantos de Daniel Svensson (5') y Viktor Gyökeres de penalti (11' y 45'). Los pupilos de Graham Potter acabaron pidiendo la hora. Armin Gigovic (47') y Sead Kolasinac (62') recortaron para los visitantes. Bosnia se tendrá que conformar con disputar la promoción de ascenso. Suecia asciende directamente. Aventajan en cinco puntos a Bosnia, en nueve a Polonia y en 10 a Rumanía.

articles.title: Clemson falls at home to Georgia Tech team that had just fired 4 coaches; Tait Reynolds exits early, Christopher Vizzina takes big hit late
articles.summary: The Yellow Jackets ended a four-game skid and secured their first win at Clemson since 2008.
articles.body:
Georgia Tech head coach Brent Key fired four coaches on Monday, namely defensive coordinator Jason Semore. The Yellow Jackets came into the weekend on a four-game losing streak and ranking toward the bottom of the FBS in several defensive categories.

At Clemson on Saturday afternoon, Key's team quieted the noise and silenced Memorial Stadium.

Tigers starting quarterback Tait Reynolds suffered a knee injury on the third play from scrimmage, and his unit never really established a rhythm without him. To make matters worse, fellow signal-caller Christopher Vizzina needed a hospital trip after a taking a big hit near the sideline late in the fourth quarter.

By game's end, Georgia Tech's beleaguered defense had held Clemson to 228 total yards in a 20-6 victory .

The Yellow Jackets (3-7, 2-5 ACC) had allowed an average of 40.3 points during their losing streak. They didn't even concede a touchdown in their first road win over the Tigers since 2008.

Clemson (6-4, 4-3) has now lost at least four games in four straight seasons. For reference, from 2012-22, Dabo Swinney's Tigers never dropped more than three contests in a season. During that span, Clemson won a pair of national titles. They haven't been in the midseason conversation for one of late, as the dialogue pertaining to the Tigers has instead fixated on whether Swinney can return his program to prominence. Clemson looked far from it on Saturday versus the Yellow Jackets.

Reynolds' injury occurred early in the matchup, near midfield. He slid at the end of a 7-yard run on Clemson's first drive of the game. After coming up hobbling, he needed assistance to get off the field. When he ultimately returned from the locker room to the sideline, he had a brace on his left knee .

Swinney said postgame that Reynold's knee "locked up on him," and that he's getting an MRI, via Chapel Fowler of The State.

Fifth-year quarterback Trent Pearman initially replaced Reynolds but threw for only 6 yards on 2-of-6 passing. Those struggles led to Swinney inserting Vizzina, the Tigers' season-opening QB1, who has recently been dealing with an ankle injury that certainly seemed to affect him throughout the game.

Vizzina connected on just 12 of his 27 attempts, finishing with 133 passing yards, no touchdowns and one interception.

That pick came with less than five minutes remaining and the Tigers trailing by two scores. The senior's overthrow was corralled by Georgia Tech safety Kealan Jones.

Later, on Clemson's final series, Vizzina absorbed a punishing blow from Yellow Jackets linebacker Cayman Spaulding while scrambling toward the sideline. That tackle took Vizzina out of the game for its remaining moments. Swinney told reporters afterward that Vizzina was headed to the hospital for a precautionary assessment of his head, neck and body .

In Vizzina's absence, Pearman filled in yet was tripped up on the subsequent fourth-and-4, resulting in the Tigers' second turnover on downs. Notably, Clemson was also shut down on a fourth-and-1 late in the opening frame. Back then, the Tigers were down 7-0, and Swinney rolled the dice from their own 34-yard line. But Pearman was denied on a sneak attempt.

Georgia Tech went on to kick a field goal to extend its lead to 10-0 in the second quarter.

The Yellow Jackets entered with the 116th-ranked rushing offense in the country, averaging 118.7 yards per game on the ground. On the road against Clemson, Georgia Tech piled up 269 rushing yards. Running back Justice Haynes collected 116 yards on 13 carries. Grady Adamson, who split time at quarterback with Alberto Mendoza, attempted just one pass but ran for 87 yards on 19 totes.

Adamson got the Yellow Jackets on the board first with a 3-yard rushing score, and Haynes broke free in the third quarter for a 53-yard TD that gave Georgia Tech a commanding 20-3 advantage.

From that point forward, Key's group hung on for the streak-snapping win at the expense of a Clemson team that was riddled by injuries at the sport's most important position.

articles.title: Romário estalla contra Ancelotti: "¡Ya fue suficiente! Agarra tus cosas y lárgate"
articles.standfirst: "No podemos arriesgarnos a tirar otro Mundial a la basura", aseguró 'O Baixinho'
articles.summary: "No podemos arriesgarnos a tirar otro Mundial a la basura", aseguró 'O Baixinho'
articles.body: Romário, leyenda del fútbol brasileño, ha pedido la dimisión del seleccionador Carlo Ancelotti tras la derrota de Brasil por 3-2, en un partido amistoso frente a Japón. "¡Ancelotti, ya fue suficiente! Agarra tus cosas y lárgate", afirmó el exjugador del Barcelona, ahora senador, en una larga publicación en redes sociales. Romário elogió al seleccionador como "uno de los grandes entrenadores" del fútbol mundial, pero aseguró que eso se limita a los clubes y no se extiende a la 'canarinha'. "Regresa a los clubes, donde te hiciste un nombre, porque la selección brasileña no puede seguir corriendo el riesgo", escribió. Además, se dirigió al presidente de la Confederación Brasileña de Fútbol, Samir Xaúd, para decirle que es el momento de demostrar que tiene "la valentía de tomar una decisión". "Ya pasamos demasiada vergüenza y no podemos arriesgarnos a tirar otro Mundial a la basura", comentó. Durante el partido, celebrado en Singapur, Japón ganó por segunda vez en la historia a Brasil con un gol de desempate en el tiempo de descuento. El propio Ancelotti fue expulsado después de reclamar una falta al árbitro de forma insistente. Contratado en 2025 y renovado en mayo pasado hasta 2030, el seleccionador ya fue criticado por el decepcionante resultado del Mundial de este año, en que Brasil fue eliminado por Noruega en octavos de final.

articles.title: Austria 1-0 Republic of Ireland: 'Painful' defeat for Republic of Ireland in Austria
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson says their 1-0 defeat against Austria in their penultimate Nations League game was "painful".
articles.body:
Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson says their 1-0 defeat by Austria in their penultimate Nations League game was "painful".

Substitute Sasa Kalajdzic poked home the winner in Linz, with the narrow victory ensuring Austria claimed top spot and automatic promotion to League A.

Chiedozie Ogbene squandered a late chance to equalise for the Republic and Hallgrimsson was frustrated they left the Raiffeisen Arena empty-handed when they had chances to secure the win which would have kept their hopes of winning the group alive.

"It was painful not to get anything from this match. I think we deserved at least a draw, but we needed the win for this game to count," he told RTE.

"I think we had the chances, the openings and the positions to do that, but this was not our day in goalscoring, so it is disappointing.

"Everything that we asked the players to do, they did and I think they gave everything.

"For that reason, we should be happy in a way but, obviously, we don't want to be building something, we want to win games."

Austria seal top spot with win over Republic of Ireland

Saturday's defeat left Hallgrimsson's side third in Group B3, a point behind Kosovo, who they face in their final game in Dublin on Tuesday.

Hallgrimsson was left to rue Republic of Ireland's inability to clear the corner from which Kalajdzic scored.

"We actually did have a lot of chances from that second ball in the box but it kind of never fell for our players in a good position," he added.

"They have a corner that they score from on the second or third touch. That's the game at this level. You need to be switched on and focused every second of the game."

Picking up a second win in the group against Kosovo would secure second place in the group which brings with it a promotion play-off and a move up to pot two for next month's Euro 2028 qualifying draw.

The Irish fell to a 1-0 defeat in Pristina in September and Hallgrimsson needs his side to finish strongly at home and pick up a vital three points.

"It was always that [Kosovo] game that was more important, but we were just so close to winning this one and being able to win the group but this is football at this level, it is all down to details."

articles.title: Dabo Swinney Reacts to 'Disappointing' Georgia Tech Loss, Updated Contract Buyout for Clemson HC
articles.summary: Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney discussed the adversity his team faces following a 20-6 loss to Georgia Tech on Saturday.
articles.body:
Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney discussed the adversity his team faces following a 20-6 loss to Georgia Tech on Saturday.

"You live in this arena, you better figure it out," Swinney told reporters. "That's just the world we're in. You go back to work, you get back up. You've got two choices: you can quit or you can get back up and go again. That's really your two options. So when you're a competitor, you put yourself in this arena, you're gonna have some good days and you're gonna have some bad days."

Biggest Coaching Buyouts in College Football History 💰

He also discussed the impact of injuries after Clemson lost quarterback Tait Reynolds to a left knee issue on the first drive of the game.

"Well it's difficult, but ain't nobody coming to save us," Swinney told reporters. "So, nobody cares. We just gotta find a way to get it done. Again, your margin for error gets smaller. We had opportunities and we didn't seize those opportunities when they did present themself."

Swinney also explained that the team plans to "evaluate everything" regarding the quarterback position moving forward.

He confirmed that he wasn't pleased with the way the Tigers battled at the line of scrimmage as well.

"I'm always embarrassed when we lose the line of scrimmage, and that's how I feel today," Swinney told reporters.

Swinney also gave his thoughts on Clemson falling to 2-9 in its last 11 home games against Power 4 opponents.

"Yeah, it's frustrating," Swinney said during his press conference . "I won't make any issues or blame it on injuries or anything like that. It's my job to get it done. It's disappointing"

As the Tigers dropped to 6-4 this season, it's worth noting that the buyout on Swinney's contract is worth $57 million (via Fox Sports ).

Clemson struggled offensively against Georgia Tech on Saturday, failing to get on the board in the first quarter before trailing 13-3 at halftime.

The Tigers only finished with a pair of field goals throughout the contest, falling to a Yellow Jackets squad that entered the game with a 2-7 record.

Clemson tallied just 14 total first downs, converting a mere five of 17 opportunities on third down. Swinney's team was also limited to 86 rush yards overall, averaging 2.5 yards per carry.

The Tigers weren't able to score a touchdown in a game for the first time this season.

While it's worth noting that Reynolds and senior quarterback Christopher Vizzina both suffered injuries against Georgia Tech on Saturday, it was still a disheartening performance by Clemson.

Swinney's overall tenure at the school has been extremely successful, owning a 193-57 record with two national championships.

However, the Tigers have steadily fallen down the ACC standings as of late. They've posted a 13-10 mark since the start of the 2025 season.

articles.title: Northern Ireland 1-0 Ukraine: The 'manager's dream' who has put NI one game from history
articles.summary: After scoring his first international goal in the 1-0 win over Ukraine, Northern Ireland boss Michael O'Neill says Terry Devlin is "a bit of a dream" to manage.
articles.body:
It was a moment that Northern Ireland needed.

When Terry Devlin picked the ball up on the edge of the area in the 68th minute against Ukraine there was only one thought in his mind.

And when the ball flew into the corner Windsor Park erupted at another highlight of a Nations League campaign that has been a real feel-good story so far.

Heading into Saturday's game they had yet to concede a goal, but the one thing they had lacked was a home win - or even a home goal - after drawing blanks in stalemates with Hungary and Georgia in Belfast.

They had already come close when Jamie Donley slotted home in the first half but the forward had strayed offside, leaving the moment the hosts had been waiting for to come through Devlin's superb winner.

It leaves Northern Ireland's Nations League fate in their own hands, and a draw or better in Hungary would secure promotion to League A for the first time.

For Northern Ireland boss Michael O'Neill, it was a huge moment from a player who he said is "a bit of a dream" to manage.

"Terry's a great lad. He deserves everything he'll get from the game and he's one of those lads that maximises what he has," O'Neill said about the 23-year-old Portsmouth defender.

Northern Ireland beat Ukraine to move closer to Nations League promotion

Devlin nets winner as NI top Nations League group

Speaking about his versatility - Devlin can play in midfield as well as a full-back on either side - O'Neill added: "He does it with no fuss. He tries to do it to the best of his ability.

"He's a bit of a dream for a manager and he has the ability to contribute goals."

The average age of O'Neill's starting XI on Saturday was just 22.9 with eight players aged 23 or younger.

Devlin epitomises what this team are all about with his all-action display rewarded with a first international goal.

A versatile option, he broke through into senior football with his hometown club Dungannon Swifts in the Irish Premiership and impressive performances for Glentoran saw him earn a move to Portsmouth in 2023.

He has now become a cult hero at Fratton Park, and he is the club's top scorer in the Championship this season.

His winner in Belfast was a fitting moment for a player who continues to grow on the international stage.

"He's a very valuable player for Portsmouth and I think he's in the process of signing a new contract there, and I imagine a lot of teams in the Championship will be disappointed by that."

While Devlin will get the headlines after his man-of-the-match performance, goalkeeper Pierce Charles came up with a big moment of his own with a superb reflex save to deny Danylo Sikan in the closing stages.

The 21-year-old has yet to concede in the Nations League campaign, and he has produced several big moments to make it 466 minutes and counting without shipping a goal for Northern Ireland.

"You don't keep five clean sheets because you're good with the ball at your feet. You keep five clean sheets because you make good decisions," said O'Neill.

"You make saves when it's needed. He kind of does it without any fuss as well, which I think is really good.

"He doesn't come and cause any issues with the back-three, which is very important for any goalkeeper, and he has a good decision-making process and a good understanding of the game."

Northern Ireland will now head to Hungary with their Nations League destiny in their own hands in what is essentially a Group B2 decider.

They are guaranteed a promotion play-off at the very least, but the goal will be to earn automatic elevation to League A for the first time.

Considering Northern Ireland had just one Nations League win in 16 League B matches before the campaign, back-to-back promotions would be a remarkable achievement.

One down side from the win over Ukraine was the two yellow cards accumulated, one for O'Neill and the other for key striker Jamie Donley.

Both were for reactions to a perceived lack of decisions from French referee Francois Letexier, and both manager and player will now watch the game in Budapest from the stands.

"The referee doesn't like my reaction and there's not much I can do about that," O'Neill said.

"I would assume that I'm going to have to watch the game from the stands, but I'll be able to influence it from there, I'm sure."

On Donley's booking, which came for protesting after Letexier failed to stop play when Trai Hume was bleeding from a cut on his head, O'Neill said it was a "poor yellow".

"I thought Jamie had a very good game for us. He'll be a blow for us," he said.

But the suspensions will do little to dampen what was another encouraging night at Windsor Park.

Hungary had piled the pressure on Northern Ireland by winning in Georgia earlier on Saturday, and Northern Ireland's response sets up a showdown to top the group on Tuesday.

"We were aware that Hungary had won the game earlier and we're in a great position," O'Neill added.

"It would be great to win the group. It will be a tough, tough game but this is a brilliant game for us. It's a great arena to play in."

Having kept five clean sheets in as many matches, O'Neill is targeting completing the campaign without conceding.

If they can do that, they would not only win promotion but secure a play-off for Euro 2028 as a back-up should their qualifying group not go to plan.

"For a nation of our size, with our players at this stage of their careers, to have a chance to win the group and also to be playing Nations League A is a big achievement.

"I think we would probably be one of the smaller nations to play at Nations League A level since the start of the competition.

"We want to try to achieve that and we have a chance to do that on Tuesday night."

articles.title: Michigan vs. Dylan Raiola, Oregon Winner, Top Box Score Player Stats & Highlights
articles.summary: Dylan Raiola and the Oregon Ducks defeated the Michigan Wolverines at Autzen Stadium on Saturday, 31-7 with the quarterback throwing three touchdown passes to lead the Ducks to victory.
articles.body:
Dylan Raiola and the Oregon Ducks defeated the Michigan Wolverines at Autzen Stadium on Saturday, 31-7 with the quarterback throwing three touchdown passes to lead the Ducks to victory.

Oregon entered its home game as a 10.5-point favorite over Michigan, per FanDuel Sportsbook , and secured the win by holding the Wolverines to just one scoring drive.

The win kept the Ducks in the hunt for the Big Ten Championship Game, improving to 7-3 on the season.

The clearest path to the championship game includes the following:

Oregon needs to win out, with its remaining games against the Michigan State Spartans and Washington Huskies.

The UCLA Bruins also need to win out to secure sole possession of first place in the Big Ten and avoid potential tiebreaker scenarios with the Ducks. UCLA holds the head-to-head tiebreaker over Oregon after defeating the Ducks earlier this season.

USC would also need to defeat the second-place Indiana Hoosiers to improve Oregon's chances of reaching the championship game. If Indiana wins against USC, the Hoosiers would need to drop one more game this season, as Oregon holds the tiebreaker over Indiana based on its record against common opponents.

Holding the tiebreaker over USC and Ohio State, Oregon would benefit from Illinois defeating Iowa and Wisconsin losing at least one of its final three games, as there are six teams with two losses in the Big Ten.

Raiola and the Ducks were hot in the first half. The quarterback, in his first year at Oregon, entered halftime 14-of-20 with 261 passing yards and three touchdowns to give Oregon a 21-7 lead.

Raiola found Jeremiah McClellan for a 60-yard touchdown pass on the Ducks' opening drive before Da'Juan Riggs caught a 2-yard touchdown pass to close out the first quarter with a 14-0 lead.

Michigan responded with a quick 24-second drive to open the second quarter, with Savion Hiter breaking off a 70-yard touchdown run. The Wolverines' defense came up with a big stop on the following drive, making a goal-line stand to keep Oregon out of the end zone.

Raiola's second deep touchdown pass came with six seconds remaining in the half, finding Dakorien Moore for a 59-yard score to cap a productive first half and give Oregon a 21-7 lead.

Michigan controlled possession in the third quarter, opening with a nearly four-minute drive before closing the period with an 8:06 drive that carried into the fourth. Both teams were held scoreless in the quarter after Oregon missed a 46-yard field goal.

It was Oregon's turn to come up with a defensive stand, shutting Michigan down in the red zone before forcing two fumbles.

Despite a penalty-filled second half for the Ducks, they put the exclamation point on the win with a 49-yard touchdown pass to Dierre Hill Jr., who finessed his way into the end zone.

Oregon will hit the road to face the Michigan State Spartans next Friday at 8 p.m. ET, while the Wolverines will host the UCLA Bruins next Saturday at a time to be determined.

articles.title: CFB Playoff Picture, Standings and Bracket Predictions After Week 11 of 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: Week 11's afternoon slate was incredibly calm compared to the bulk of the 2026 college football season.
articles.body:
Week 11's afternoon slate was incredibly calm compared to the bulk of the 2026 college football season.

No major upsets took place, which meant top-10 teams were able to solidify their respective resumes with victories.

The Indiana Hoosiers picked up the most significant win on Saturday afternoon with a home win over the USC Trojans. That was Indiana's first Top 25 win of the campaign.

There's potential for Week 11 to have some upsets, though, as the No. 2 Utah Utes and No. 6 Texas Longhorns both play on the road on Saturday night.

The CFB Playoff projections are based off the results after Week 11's afternoon games.

The Indiana Hoosiers answered some critics on Saturday with a home win over the USC Trojans.

Indiana dropped five spots in Tuesday's CFB Playoff ranking mainly because of its low strength of schedule.

Before Saturday, all eight of Indiana's victories came against unranked opponents. Its only loss, to the Ohio State Buckeyes, looks worse because of OSU's recent slide.

The victory over USC should help Indiana's resume in the eyes of the CFB Playoff selection committee.

Indiana now has a very clear path to the playoff field. It just needs to beat the Washington Huskies and Purdue Boilermakers in the next two weeks.

If that happens, the Hoosiers will most likely meet the UCLA Bruins in the Big Ten Championship Game. Indiana could be playing for a first-round bye in the playoffs in that potential matchup depending on what happens over the next few weeks to the teams above it.

As for USC, Saturday marked the end of its playoff dream, but it could still play spoiler in two weeks against UCLA.

No. 8 Tennessee Picks Up Road Win At Texas A&M

The Tennessee Volunteers passed their last big road test of the regular season against the Texas A&M Aggies.

The eighth-ranked Vols are now 8-2 with two games left. The next game is a home meeting with the LSU Tigers. The regular-season finale is a road trip to face the Vanderbilt Commodores.

Getting to 10-2 is important for the Vols because that would basically guarantee their spot in the 12-team playoff field.

Josh Heupel's team still has a shot at the SEC Championship Game as well depending on how the tiebreakers shake out. The Vols own head-to-head wins over the Alabama Crimson Tide and Kentucky Wildcats, two of the other three two-loss teams in SEC play.

A 10-2 record with a SEC Championship Game berth, which would likely come with a matchup against the top-ranked Georgia Bulldogs, should be more than enough for the Vols to feel safe inside the playoff field.

articles.title: No. 9 Indiana ends No. 18 USC's chances of making the College Football Playoff in 27-13 win
articles.summary: USC got within 10 yards of the end zone on three straight second-half drives and came away with three points.
articles.body:
USC's red-zone woes are why it has no hope of making the College Football Playoff .

The No. 18 Trojans got within 10 yards of the end zone on three straight second-half drives on Saturday at No. 9 Indiana. And all they got from those drives were a measly three points in a 27-13 loss to the Hoosiers.

On the third drive, USC (7-3) was at the Indiana 6-yard line while trailing 20-13. On second down, QB Jayden Maiava threw toward the end zone and apparently never saw linebacker Isaiah Jones, who stepped in front of the pass before it had any chance of being completed.

Seven plays later, Indiana (9-1) had a two-score lead. Grant Wilson, starting in place of Josh Hoover, found Charlie Becker in single coverage for a 42-yard TD on third down with 3:30 to go.

After that, USC's chances of a comeback were near zero. And they quickly became zero when Maiava threw his third interception of the game with 2:24 remaining.

On the drive before Maiava's second interception, USC got to the 10-yard line. But a run for no gain and a third-down incompletion made coach Lincoln Riley call for a 27-yard field goal. But Camden Chittenden's kick from the right hash never moved left enough to get inside the uprights.

Indiana scores its most points in over a month

In his postgame interview with CBS, Indiana coach Curt Cignetti said that Hoover was "healthy" entering Saturday's game. But he opted to start Wilson, a seventh-year senior who made his first start since the 2024 season.

Wilson finished the game 17-of-27 passing for 305 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. He threw a touchdown on Indiana's opening drive of the game and the Hoosiers' offense stalled after that.

However, Indiana scored on three of its first four drives of the second half before kneeling out the clock.

RBs Khobie Martin and Lee Beebe Jr. combined to rush 28 times for 153 yards and a score, while Becker had three grabs for 75 yards.

Before Saturday, Indiana hadn't scored more than 23 points in any of its last four games. And it only broke 20 because of overtime in Week 10 when it beat Minnesota 23-16. Those offensive struggles were a big reason why Indiana dropped from No. 5 to No. 9 in the second set of CFP rankings even though the Hoosiers didn't play in Week 10.

It also didn't help that all of the Big Ten teams Indiana has beaten this season all lost in Week 10. And none of those teams was ranked, anyway. But now Indiana has a conference win over a ranked team. The committee could easily re-evaluate the Hoosiers ahead of Tuesday night's latest rankings.

The Trojans are now 0-8 under Riley against ranked teams in games played outside of Los Angeles after Saturday's loss. And they're also guaranteed to finish the season with at least three losses. No USC team during Riley's five years in charge has lost fewer than three games in a season.

It's yet another example of just how far away USC is from being a contender in the Big Ten. USC simply has a hard time winning away from the West Coast. And that's a problem when most of the teams in your conference are multiple time zones away.

Since joining the Big Ten, USC is 4-6 in conference games in either the Central or Eastern Time Zone. Its only wins have come over Purdue and Nebraska in 2025 and Rutgers and Penn State in 2026.

Increased travel is the trade you make when you switch conferences for a larger payday. Yet it's also not the only explanation for USC's struggles. This season, USC entered Week 11 scoring on just 82% of its red-zone possessions. According to Team Rankings, that's 89th among 138 FBS teams.

The offense and the defense have rarely showed up at the same time against good competition, either. In a 24-7 loss to Wisconsin, USC finished with negative rushing yards. Against Oregon, the defense was picked apart for 504 yards on 58 plays.

The inability to show that USC can be a top team in the Big Ten is a big reason why Riley made such an emphatic display before and after the Ohio State game of saying why he wanted to be at USC. But as the Trojans stare at another disappointing season, is Riley's future really going to be decided on his terms?

articles.title: Folarin Balogun Explains Hitting Damian Lillard Celebration After Goal for USMNT vs. Haiti on Video
articles.summary: Folarin Balogun says he was inspired by Portland Trail Blazers star Damian Lillard when celebrating his first USMNT goal since the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
articles.body:
Folarin Balogun says he was inspired by Portland Trail Blazers star Damian Lillard when celebrating his first USMNT goal since the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Balogun tapped his wrist in imitation of Lillard's signature "Dame Time" celebration after scoring against Haiti during Saturday's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal in Maimi.

"After the World Cup has been a bit of a up-and-down period for me, so it's just nice to come back here with the boys, get the win, and get a goal," Balogun told TNT Sports' Melissa Ortiz after the game.

"Just giving homage to Damian Lillard, Dame Time. I wanted to kind of show it's just my time. I'm back."

The nod to Lillard comes after the star returned from a season lost to an Achilles injury to help lead the Trail Blazers to a 9-3 start.

Balogun's goal marked the final tally of a 6-0 blowout over Haiti that allowed the United States to clinch a spot in the Concacaf Nations League semifinals.

The game took place in Balogun's first game back with the USMNT since he became a central figure in the USMNT's trip to the World Cup's Round of 16.

He followed up that run by pursuing an ultimately failed transfer from the French Club AS Monaco to the Premier League's Everton. Balogun has since seen limited playing time with Monaco, which he said he plans to transfer from in January, per ESPN's Jeff Carlisle .

Balogun could now look to ride the momentum of his return to the United States scoresheet as the USMNT heads to Cincinnati for the second leg of the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal, which will mark manager Mauricio Pochettino's final game with the team before he leaves to coach Manchester United.

articles.title: 'Obrigado, capi7ão': All Portugal players wear Ronaldo's No. 7,  jersey immortalised with a permanent change in special tribute to Cristiano
articles.summary: Portugal paid tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo in their first match since the forward announced his retirement from international football, with every player
articles.body: Portugal paid tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo in their first match since the forward announced his retirement from international football, with every player wearing his iconic No. 7 jersey before their UEFA Nations League clash against Denmark on Saturday.The tribute extended beyond the players, with the young mascots accompanying them also wearing the No. 7 shirt. Supporters in the stands displayed a banner reading "Obrigado, capi7ão" — "Thank you, captain" — alongside images of Ronaldo lifting the European Championship and Nations League trophies.Portugal also made a change to the way the No. 7 is written on their shirts to honour Ronaldo's legacy. The new design features a horizontal line crossing through the number, similar to the way Ronaldo used to write it.“Time to debut a new 7. Because there's one that will be eternal,” the Portuguese national team wrote on social media on Saturday. The post also included a goat emoji, referring to Ronaldo as the Greatest Of All Time.The change ensures that Ronaldo's version of the No. 7 remains distinct from those who wear the number in the future. The forward made the number his identity during his career, becoming known as 'CR7'.Ronaldo announced his international retirement on November 5, bringing an end to a career with Portugal that spanned 23 years. He made 246 appearances for his country and scored 146 goals, becoming the men's all-time leading international goalscorer.He captained Portugal to their first major international trophy at Euro 2016 and also helped them win the Nations League in 2019 and 2025. His international career included appearances at six FIFA World Cups.The tribute came nine days after his retirement announcement. Ronaldo's last appearance for Portugal was on September 24, in a 1-0 home win over Wales in the Nations League.However, the celebrations before the Denmark match were followed by a disappointing result for Portugal. Playing their first game without Ronaldo, they suffered a 4-1 home defeat, with Rasmus Hojlund scoring twice for Denmark.In the other League A Group Four match, Norway beat Wales 3-1 in Oslo. Antonio Nusa and Andreas Schjelderup scored before Erling Haaland converted a late penalty to complete the win.Despite the defeat, Portugal remain at the top of the group with 12 points, three ahead of Denmark. Norway are third with six points, while Wales are at the bottom with three.One round of league-phase matches remains. articles.title: Mike Bianchi: Miami’s win over Duke is impressive, but its 22-year ACC championship drought is downright embarrassing!
articles.summary: Before fifth-ranked Miami starts making hotel reservations for the College Football Playoff and another trip to the national championship game, perhaps the H...
articles.body:
Before fifth-ranked Miami starts making hotel reservations for the College Football Playoff and another trip to the national championship game, perhaps the Hurricanes should accomplish something they've failed to do for 22 embarrassing years.

For all the swagger, all the tradition, all the five national championships and all the incessant talk about restoring The U to its rightful place among college football's elite, Miami has never won an ACC championship.

That's not merely disappointing. It's arguably the most humiliating non-achievement in the history of a football program that once measured success in national championships, not conference participation trophies.

Which brings us to Saturday's impressive 36-25 victory over Duke, a good football team coached by former Miami coach Manny Diaz. A week after a gut-wrenching loss to Notre Dame, the fifth-ranked Hurricanes responded the way championship contenders are supposed to respond.

Quarterback Darian Mensah, facing his former school, threw for 382 yards. Running back Javian Mallory scored three touchdowns, including a spectacular 63-yard catch-and-run and a 39-yard fourth-quarter sprint that finally put away the stubborn Blue Devils.

Miami improved to 9-1 overall and 7-0 in the ACC, extending its conference winning streak to 11 games and matching a school record. More importantly, Miami is the only unbeaten team in ACC play with two regular-season games remaining.

The Hurricanes are practically assured a trip to the conference championship game, needing just one more victory against overmatched competition to officially punch their ticket. And that's where the real pressure begins.

Because while everybody seems fascinated by Miami's national championship possibilities, there's a rather inconvenient piece of unfinished business sitting right in front of the Hurricanes.

Remember what was supposed to happen when Miami joined the conference in 2004? Miami and Florida State were going to become the Ohio State and Michigan of the ACC. Two glamorous, nationally relevant football factories whose annual battles would elevate the conference into a television gold mine.

Instead, the ACC got something closer to a 22-year bait-and-switch. Miami has delivered precisely zero conference championships. Florida State has enjoyed considerably more success, including a national championship in 2013, but has also endured long stretches of embarrassing irrelevance.

Meanwhile, both schools have complained that the ACC hasn't delivered the television riches flowing into the SEC and Big Ten. And they have a point. But here's a question nobody in Coral Gables or Tallahassee particularly wants to answer:

Hasn't Miami and FSU let down the ACC more than ACC has down Miami and FSU?

Imagine if Miami and Florida State had spent the past two decades doing what Alabama and Georgia have done in the SEC — competing for national championships, dominating television ratings and turning ordinary conference Saturdays into must-see events. Would the ACC's television deal look quite so pathetic today?

The SEC didn't become college football's financial monster because of clever conference-office marketing. It became a monster because its marquee programs consistently delivered the product. Championship football sells. Nostalgia doesn't. Miami has spent far too many years selling a dynasty that exists only in the rearview mirror.

And now, finally, the Hurricanes have an opportunity to deliver something more substantial.

If the ACC championship game were played today, Miami would face 11th-ranked Wake Forest, which announced itself as a legitimate threat Saturday by dismantling SMU 49-7. That's not some ceremonial opponent showing up to congratulate Miami on its return to relevance. That's a potential championship opponent capable of ruining the coronation.

And Miami shouldn't need reminding that Duke won the ACC championship last season with Mensah at quarterback. If Duke can win this league, surely Miami can figure out how to do it at least once in 22 years.

The urgency is even greater because this is the final season of the ACC championship game. Beginning next year, college football's expanded 24-team playoff will eliminate conference championship games, replacing the drama of settling championships on the field with standings, complicated tiebreakers and mathematical gymnastics.

Conference champions will still be crowned, but the spectacle of two teams meeting with a trophy on the line will disappear. Miami, therefore, has one last opportunity to win an ACC championship the old-fashioned way. By beating somebody for it.

And what a delicious irony it would be if the Hurricanes finally captured their first ACC crown in the conference's final championship game. Twenty-two years of frustration erased in one December afternoon.

Of course, that wouldn't automatically make Miami a national champion. It wouldn't guarantee a playoff victory or restore the dynasty that once terrorized college football. But it would eliminate an embarrassment that has hung around this program like an unpaid parking ticket.

Coach Mario Cristobal has assembled a team talented enough to dream about winning everything. Mensah looks like a championship quarterback. The offense has explosive playmakers — even with the loss of the injured Malachi Toney. The Hurricanes have survived the grind of conference competition without a loss.

That's worth celebrating. But Miami hasn't earned the right to skip a step.

National championships are the ultimate ambition. Conference championships are supposed to be the minimum expectation for programs that consider themselves national powers. For 22 years, Miami has failed to meet even that standard.

So enough with the national championship chatter for now. Win the ACC. Then talk about conquering America.

Before Miami can reclaim its place atop college football, it needs to prove it can finally finish atop its own conference.

articles.title: Faizon Brandon explains his relationship now with Tennessee QB George MacIntyre
articles.summary: Tennessee quarterback Faizon Brandon said his relationship with George MacIntyre has grown stronger as the season has progressed.
articles.body:
Tennessee football started its season with a quarterback competition between Faizon Brandon and George MacIntyre. Now they are both playing a role in the November push for a College Football Playoff berth.

Brandon is embracing Tennessee coach Josh Heupel's willingness to play both quarterbacks as needed, and the strategy that has played a key role in wins over Kentucky and Texas A&M in consecutive weeks.

"I think I we have a way better relationship now than we did back then," Brandon said after Tennessee defated the Aggies 22-7 on Nov. 14 in College Station, Texas. "We're talking a lot more I feel like we're a lot more connected and know that we need each other."

Tennessee football, George MacIntyre vs Texas A&M, see our best photos | Exclusive

As the No. 9 Vols (8-2, 5-2 SEC) grinded through the victory against Texas A&M (4-6, 1-6), Heupel needed contributions from both MacIntyre, the sophomore who made his fifth consecutive start and Brandon, the five-star freshman who started the first five games.

MacIntyre had completed 66% of his passes for 705 yards, one touchdown and three interceptions in his four previous starts. In his five starts, Brandon had completed 60% of his passes for 697 yards, seven touchdowns and one interception, while also rushing for 130 yards and three touchdowns.

However, MacIntyre suffered a knee injury and exited the game in the third quarter, allowing for Brandon to see his first extended action since returning from a shoulder injury he suffered in the loss to Texas on Sept. 26 and being benched in the second quarter of the Auburn win the following week.

"Really, I was just trying to get healthy first and then stay prepared, wait my turn, keep on preparing and learning like I got the starting job," Brandon said.

Neither player was prolific as the Vols won behind 175 combined rushing yards from DeSean Bishop and Javin Gordon, and a suffocating defense that allowed only 179 total yards.

"George got twisted up on the one pass play and comes back in and was battling through it but had to go back (to the sideline). But with where the game was, just didn't feel like it was the right place for George, just dealing with that injury," coach Josh Heupel said. "Both of them played extremely well. Proud of both of those guys. Big smiles on their faces. Excited about the win. They care about the team and straining and competing."

MacIntyre completed his first 10 throws and exited having completed 13 of 17 passes for 109 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions.

Brandon, who was used in specialty packages for the Vols during their win over Kentucky, was in for only a handful of run plays in the first half.

Brandon completed one pass, but it was Tennessee's only touchdown in the game, a 5-yard strike to tight end DaSaahn Brame at the 10:13 mark of the third quarter. He also rushed six times for 36 yards and used his legs to seal the win in the fourth quarter.

"Kind of got the jitters out early, so when I went in, it was just getting with the flow of the game," Brandon said about his early snaps in place of MacIntyre. "So I did feel like it helped me out early."
